items.item_text: For questions regarding this position, please contact the Human Resources Department at hr@frc.edu .
Visa Sponsorship
H1B1 visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
Current California active license as a Registered Nurse or Licensed Vocational Nurse.
Current active CA license as an RN.
A bachelor’s degree in any subject, plus two years of professional experience directly related to the teaching assignment
an associate degree in any subject, plus six years of professional experience directly related to the teaching assignment.
Baccalaureate degree in nursing from an approved school.
Have a minimum of two years’ experience as an RN or LVN within the last five years.
Teaching experience at the college level, preferably community college.
Experience in high and low fidelity simulation, scenario development, skills lab use; may include moulage, equipment and software maintenance, P&P development.

Teach and develop curriculum for the college’s Vocational Nursing Program. An example of courses currently in the curriculum include: Certified Nurse Assistant; Medical Dosage Calculations; Medical Terminology; Nursing Foundations and Lab; Mental Health Nursing; Introduction to Pharmacology; Basic, Intermediate, and Advanced Medical Surgical Nursing and Labs; Transition to Nursing Practice; and IV Therapy and Blood Withdrawal.

Support the Allied Health Director in researching and developing curriculum for the Allied Health Program which may include low and high-fidelity simulations, emergency medical technician, CPR and/or first aid, phlebotomy, home health aide, medical assisting, medical office technology, and medical billing and coding, independently or in conjunction with other schools.

Create and implementing culturally responsive, accessible, and equity minded course material, teaching practices, and learning assessment strategies that enhance student success and persistence toward academic/career goals and that help close equity gaps.
Demonstrate and maintain proficiency in the college’s learning management system consistent with district policies and instructional responsibilities.
Assist with the supervision and coordination of Allied Health Program in conformance with applicable state regulations, requirements, accreditation standards and state and college policies.

Participate in activities such as lab organization, course scheduling, budget creation, purchasing supplies, conducting evaluations, and reporting on program and course level student learning outcomes.
Participate in the recruitment and selection of nursing faculty.

Assist with required reports and approval forms for the California Board of Vocational Nursing and Psychiatric Technicians and Feather River College as well as other related agencies such as Nor-Cal EMS and the California Department of Public Health, if applicable.
Assist with maintaining contractual agreements and clinical schedules with community service agencies used as clinical sites for Allied Health Program students.

Participate in college duties such as scheduled office hours, curriculum development, selection of textbooks, evaluation of course materials, committee membership, student advising, program promotion, and college and community service.
Prepare recruitment materials, participating in recruitment activities, and conducting activities that support student retention.
Participate in professional growth activities in order to remain current in the discipline and maintain applicable professional licenses and certifications.
Other duties as assigned.

Medical-surgical nursing; teaching principles and methods and their impact on the learning process; curriculum development; Nursing Education trends and issues; nursing theory; supervisory techniques; professional standards of conduct and ethics in the nursing profession; laboratory equipment operation, uses, and precautions.
Successful completion of courses in teaching, curriculum development, and administration from an approved school.

Lecture and otherwise instruct students in the classroom AND practice laboratory AND clinical settings; exercise skill in fundamentals of nursing and the practice of medical-surgical nursing; instruct in fundamentals of nursing and medical-surgical nursing; supervise students in the clinical setting; contribute to curriculum development; form and maintain positive, supportive relationships with students to facilitate learning; maintain accurate student records; work cooperatively with peers, other faculty, staff, and students; teach in registered and vocational nursing and Nursing Assistant programs; work some evenings and/or weekends, as required; write course objectives, outlines, and lesson plans; prepare course syllabi; communicate effectively orally and in writing; follow oral and written instructions; function as a team member; maintain positive relationships with external clinical agencies; maintain professional standards of conduct and ethics; function as a professional role model; participate in student, faculty, shared governance, and professional activities; exercise appropriate safety precautions in practice laboratory and clinical settings; type/keyboard and/or utilize mouse to operate microcomputers to utilize software packages/applications for word processing.
Knowledge of BVNPT rules and regulations that govern undergraduate professional vocational nursing educational programs; pre-licensure program curriculum and instructional program development.
Ability to research and locate alternative funding sources; ability to locate and apply to potential foundation or grant funding sources.
